Using transformer-based architectures, including attention-based models, the purpose of this research is to establish an automatic approach for reconstructing noisy EEG channels. There were three different noise scenarios that were taken into consideration, and they were zero-mashing, noise masking, and zero-noise masking. The reconstructing model combines convulsion neural networks (CNN) with a multi-head self attehtion transformer model. We designed the model to balance both performance and sustainability considerations. The findings indicate that the model was able to accomplish a high level of reconstructing skills, as indicated by the value of R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, which is equivalent to 0.8563 within a margin of error of 0.0543. In addition, considerations of sustainability were taken into account for the actual execution where the model size was restricted to less than 0.5 MB.

articleTitle: Enhancing E-Book Reading: Integration Text to Speech and BART Model Summarization
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computing, Engineering and Design (ICCED)
abstract: Reading is the main foundation of the continuous learning process and a universal right for every individual. Reading activities provide access to new knowledge, broaden the mind, and broaden horizons. Along with technological advances, digital books or e-books have become an important alternative to traditional printed books. E-books not only provide text but also images, videos, and audio that can be accessed through electronic devices. To maximize the potential of e-books, integration of technologies such as text-to-speech systems and text summarization is needed. The text-to-speech system allows users to listen to e-book content, while text summarization using the BART method conveys complex information without losing its essence. The application of this technology on the AllInclusiveReads platform is expected to help people who have limitations in visual abilities or reading long texts and can improve the user's reading experience. Considering the test findings with the evaluation method, the best result was obtained in the calculation of the Rouge 1 monogram overlap, which was 0.5735 for the Precision value, 0.4615 for the recall value and 0.5477 for the F1 score value. This research will be developed in the future so that it can not only process PDF files, but also other formats. This research will be developed in the future using other methods, so that it can not only process PDF document files, but also other formats.

articleTitle: Smart IoT-Driven Shopping Assistance System for Cognitive Impairment Patients: Ensuring Safe and Independent Shopping Experiences
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computing, Engineering and Design (ICCED)
abstract: Cognitive impairment patients face challenges in managing daily tasks due to memory and cognitive issues. IoT solutions play a crucial role in helping them navigate complex environments such as retail settings, promoting both autonomy and security. This research paper presents an IoT-Driven Smart Shopping Assistance System designed to improve the shopping experience for individuals with cognitive impairments. The system features a wearable IoT device equipped with RFID-based product identification for accurate item recognition, GPS for live tracking of the patient's location, and a secure NFC payment system using two-factor authentication (2FA) with a password and facial recognition. By integrating ‘Smart-Cart’ technology, the device displays items from a caregiver-managed database as the patient approaches them, providing real-time, location-based shopping assistance. The NFC payment system enforces a spending limit, requiring caregiver approval for larger purchases to prevent financial mishandling. Additionally, Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) ensures continuous connectivity, enabling caregivers to receive real-time alerts in case of confusion or emergencies such falls. This comprehensive system empowers patients to shop independently while maintaining their safety, making it a scalable and adaptable solution for various retail environments.

articleTitle: Experimental Results for Mushroom-Based Dye Sensitized Solar Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computing, Engineering and Design (ICCED)

authors.preferredName: Wan Abd Al Qadr Imad Wan-Mohtar

abstract: This study explores the usage of novel oyster mushroom dyes in dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) as photosensitizer to substitute the costly chemical dyes with a more eco-friendly, natural alternatives. Utilization of oyster mushroom dye as a natural dye for DSSC is due to their large biomass yield and the fact that they can be cultivated in a regulated environment. Dye from pink oyster mushroom was extracted and dried using freeze-drying methods. Characterization involved I-V measurements for electrical properties, UV-Vis spectrophotometry for optical analysis, and testing using solar simulator for current density-voltage (J-V) characterization. Freeze-dried pink mushroom dyes showed optimal properties for DSSCs, with energy bandgaps of between 1.71 and 2.14 eV The fabricated DSSC performance was determined using a solar simulator, and the fabricated DSSC device exhibited an efficiency of 0.107%.

articleTitle: The Convergence of AI and Wireless Communication System in Modern Aquaculture: A Systematic Review
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computing, Engineering and Design (ICCED)
abstract: This research examines the synergy between artificial intelligence (AI) technology and wireless communication in aquaculture through the Systematic Literature Review (SLR) method. With the increasing demand for fishery products, aquaculture offers a sustainable solution to meet global food needs. The problem faced is the need for sustainable solutions to meet the growing demand for fishery products. The methods used include data collection from the Scopus database, the use of PRISMA diagrams for literature selection, and data analysis using RStudio, resulting in 36 documents analyzed. The research results show that AI and wireless communication technology have great potential in improving the efficiency and productivity of aquaculture. The integration of AI and wireless communication allows real-time monitoring of environmental conditions and fish health, increasing efficiency and productivity. The contribution of this research is to provide a comprehensive insight into how this technology can improve aquaculture yields and product quality, as well as identify challenges in its implementation.

articleTitle: Development and Evaluation of an AI-Driven Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) Model for Automated Pneumonia Detection Using Chest X-Ray Image
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computing, Engineering and Design (ICCED)
abstract: Pneumonia remains a leading cause of mortality globally, especially in low-resource settings where timely and accurate diagnosis is often not readily available. Chest X-ray (CXR) imaging is a critical tool for pneumonia diagnosis; however, its interpretation depends heavily on the expertise of radiologists, which can introduce variability. This study presents a computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) system based on a convolutional neural network (CNN) designed to automatically classify CXR images as either normal or indicative of pneumonia. The CNN model was evaluated across 10, 20, 50, and 100 epochs, achieving a peak accuracy of 92%, a precision-recall score of 95%, and an AUC of 96%. Notably, the model demonstrated strong performance without the need for advanced preprocessing techniques such as Dynamic Histogram Equalization (DHE) or Histogram Equalization (HE). Despite the simplicity of the approach, the model maintained competitive performance, with a precision of 93% observed at 50 epochs. Further analysis through precision-recall and ROC curves confirmed the model's consistent and reliable performance across all evaluated epochs. This CNN-based approach provides an efficient solution for pneumonia detection in clinical settings, particularly in regions with limited access to radiologists. It holds significant potential to improve diagnostic accuracy, particularly in under-resourced areas.

articleTitle: Bi-Directional DC-DC Converter for Enhanced Power Management in Electric Vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computing, Engineering and Design (ICCED)
abstract: The increasing adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) as a sustainable and efficient alternative to conventional gasoline-powered vehicles highlights the critical need for a reliable and effective charging infrastructure. This paper introduces an advanced control strategy for a power-split hybrid transmission system, which integrates a bi-directional DC-DC converter to optimize power management in hybrid and electric vehicle applications. The system architecture, incorporating a planetary gear system alongside motor and generator components, functions as a variable ratio gear, enabling smooth and efficient energy distribution. MATLAB/Simulink simulations assessed the system's performance under acceleration and regenerative braking conditions, highlighting the converter's ability to manage energy flow effectively between the battery and motor. The research investigates the differences between isolated and non-isolated DC-DC converters, highlighting the benefits of both designs in a variety of applications. Isolated converters improve safety and noise isolation; however, non-isolated systems are more compact and cost-effective. The results demonstrate the proposed system's ability to utilize electrical power exclusively during vehicle maneuvers, optimize energy efficiency, and reduce reliance on mechanical power. This research underscores the potential for advanced DC-DC converter topologies to enhance power management strategies in hybrid systems, providing valuable insights for future innovations in energy storage, power conversion, and electric vehicle technologies.

articleTitle: Detecting Lateral Movement in Advanced Persistent Threats Based on Remote Desktop Protocol
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computing, Engineering and Design (ICCED)
abstract: Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs) are one of the most perilous forms of cyberattacks, partly because they concentrate on certain, high-value targets. A pivotal stage in these assaults is lateral movement, wherein attackers traverse compromised systems to acquire additional control and access sensitive information. This study concentrates on identifying lateral movement in Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs), particularly via the Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) as a principal attack vector, especially in 2019 with Corona pandemic increasing the work online It has become necessary to protect the network, its accessories, and the devices connected to it to ensure protected access and prevent hacking. Deep learning models were utilized to detect malicious behavior with event logs LANL dataset, and the model's efficacy was assessed using conventional metrics like F1-score, precision, recall, and accuracy. We have attained a performance level of 99.98% with CNN and RNN.

articleTitle: Learning to Generate and Predict New Conditional Small Organic Molecules
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computing, Engineering and Design (ICCED)
abstract: Organic molecules are essential in various fields, including drug discovery, pharmaceuticals, materials science, and agrochemicals. However, synthesizing new organic molecules in laboratories is both costly and time-intensive. This paper introduces a novel approach for generating and predicting new conditional small organic molecules. The approach utilizes a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN), specifically a Wasserstein GAN (WGAN), to generate new molecular structures, and a Vision Transformer (ViT) to classify these generated molecules. To ensure the organic compounds generated are chemically feasible, the WGAN is conditioned with specific parameters, such as bond types and elemental composition. A generated dataset, named GenOrgo, includes 400 new molecules categorized into four classes: Homocycles, Heterocycles, Oxygen- and Nitrogen-containing Acyclics, and Hydrocarbons. The ViT is then evaluated on the GenOrgo dataset, demonstrating its effectiveness in accurately predicting the categories of generated organic molecules. The code and the dataset are available at github.com/RaghadAllehyani/WGAN.

articleTitle: Impact of Image Resolution on Convolutional Neural Networks for Alzheimer Disease Dataset Classification: A ResNet Study
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computing, Engineering and Design (ICCED)
abstract: Reducing image resolution can save computing resources but may result in loss of details. Understanding the relationship between image resolution and the performance of various CNN architectures is crucial for setting standards in CNN -based model properties. This study investigates CNN performance on the Kaggle Alzheimer's dataset, comprising 6,400 images divided into four sections representing disease progression stages. We evaluated the ResNet CNN variants models for image classification using resolutions of 64x64, 128x128, and 256x256 pixels. Performance was assessed using evaluation metrics including Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F -Measure, Loss and Time of execution. Optimal performance, with the highest evaluation metric values, was observed with the highest resolution (256x256 pixels), achieving classification of the entire dataset, including all subclasses. This highlights the significant influence of image resolution on CNN models performance. Moreover, resolution affects the computational time and complexity of calculations. As an example of the results, among the best performances obtained, the ResNet-101 model with a resolution of 256x256 achieved an accuracy of 97.08%, a precision of 97.76%, a recall of 98.13%, and an F -measure of 97.94<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, with a loss of 0.045. However, the average execution time per epoch is about 75 seconds, which is a significant time.

articleTitle: Crime Time-Series Forecasting in Indonesia Using Neural Network and Linear Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computing, Engineering and Design (ICCED)
abstract: Crime is a harmful and widespread social issue affecting individuals globally, including in Indonesia, requiring not only reactive but also predictive measures for effective prevention. Lack of continuously updated official crime information and predictions can lead to a variety of adverse outcomes. Without current data, law enforcement agencies may struggle to allocate resources effectively, potentially leaving some communities underserved and vulnerable. Public safety could be compromised as patterns of criminal activity shift without being detected in real-time, preventing the implementation of proactive measures. Furthermore, the absence of accurate predictions hampers the ability to forecast and prepare for possible crime waves or emerging threats. This deficiency can also undermine public trust in law enforcement's capacity to protect citizens and maintain order. This research employed data mining and machine learning methods to forecast crime trends in Indonesia. The approach depends on continuously refreshed and accurate data derived from public court rulings. Data from the Supreme Court of Indonesia was gathered, stored, and pre-processed, after which various machine learning models were utilized to produce crime time-series forecasting. These predictions aim to provide law enforcement and the society with actionable insights for targeted crime prevention, enhancing public safety and preparedness. This research demonstrates the potential of data mining and machine learning in accurately predicting crimes, supporting efforts to safeguard society.

articleTitle: Model of Artificial Intelligence Utilization Among Financial Auditors
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computing, Engineering and Design (ICCED)
abstract: In the era of Industry 4.0, auditors face increasing workloads and tight deadlines, making the adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) crucial for enhancing efficiency and accuracy. This study aims to analyze the factors influencing AI utilization among auditors by employing a modified Model of PC Utilization. The research involves auditors working in public accounting firms in Jakarta, with data analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS). The research findings show that social factors, perceived complexity, perceived job fit, perceived long term consequence and facilitating conditions each has significant effect on auditor utilization of artificial intelligence, however in contrary affect has no significant effect. The study contributes to the academic discourse on technology adoption in auditing, offering new and significant results that highlight the importance of practical and social factors in AI integration.

articleTitle: A Comparison Study of the Existing Requirements Ambiguity Detection Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computing, Engineering and Design (ICCED)
abstract: Software requirements ambiguity is a common issue that can lead to miscommunication, project delays, and increased costs. This paper provides an extensive evaluation of existing frameworks designed to detect ambiguity in requirements engineering. Through comparison and analysis, the study assesses the methods, advantages, and disadvantages of various frameworks. The results highlight the effectiveness of the existing approaches and identify areas in which more investigation and enhancement are needed. The significance of identifying ambiguity to enhance the quality of software requirements is emphasized by this investigation. It also offers important insights for further advancement in this field. With an emphasis on improving the quality of requirements, the study's contributions are intended to help practitioners and researchers improve the efficiency and reliability of requirements engineering techniques.

articleTitle: Enhancing Autonomous Vehicle Safety Through Collaborative Robotic Features
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computing, Engineering and Design (ICCED)
abstract: Nowadays, the automotive industry stands at the forefront of transformative change. This paper focuses on augmenting modern automobiles with collaborative robotic features, specifically emphasizing robot-robot collaboration through a multi-robot system. The proposed approach envisions vehicles communicating crucial information to nearby counterparts, fostering a collective response to potential threats and hazards on the road. The proposed prototype comprises a master-slave configuration involving two cars, where the master car transmits vital information to the slave car, guiding its actions based on real-time environmental data. This communication empowers the master car to proactively alert the slave car to obstacles and propose optimal solutions while both vehicles are in motion. The primary objective is to successfully develop a prototype that enables vehicles to share information, facilitating adaptive navigation and obstacle avoidance. Aligned with Vehicle-to-everything (V2X) technology, this research uses Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) communication as a practical implementation of intervehicular collaboration. The anticipated outcome is a tangible contribution to the advancement of autonomous vehicle safety by harnessing real-time communication for dynamic hazard mitigation. This research contributes to the ongoing evolution of autonomous vehicles, enhancing their safety and responsiveness in complex driving scenarios.

articleTitle: Mapping the Research Landscape : A Bibliometric Study of Flow Rate Sensors and Horizontal Water Pipe
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computing, Engineering and Design (ICCED)
abstract: The significance of flow rate sensors and horizontal water pipes in various applications highlights their crucial role in enhancing fluid dynamics monitoring and management. This study aims to map the research landscape through a bibliometric analysis of flow rate sensors and horizontal water pipes. The analysis includes author analysis, affiliation analysis, country or territory analysis, source analysis, keyword analysis, trend topic analysis, and thematic map analysis. Bibliometric analysis helps policymakers, industry professionals, and researchers navigate the extensive body of literature, ensuring that efforts in flow rate sensor technology and horizontal water pipe research align with current trends and contribute effectively to advancing knowledge in these areas. The results will serve as a valuable guide, helping stakeholders understand the evolving research landscape, make informed decisions, and gain deeper insights into the trajectory of research in flow rate sensors and horizontal water pipes.

articleTitle: A Variable Neighborhood Search Combined with EM Clustering and Classification: Application to Credit Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computing, Engineering and Design (ICCED)
abstract: Data mining involves a range of techniques designed to improve logistics and supply chain management. It has great significance and importance in logistics enterprises. It can be used in production, transportation, supplier selection and warehousing. Also, it can optimize the supplier selection, facility location, vehicle routing and help managers in decision making. Clustering, or partitioning, is a prominent task in data mining aimed at dividing large datasets into homogeneous groups, where items within the same group exhibit similarity. This work focuses on credit scoring to assist banks and managers in their decision-making processes. We use Expectation-Maximization (EM) clustering to categorize applicants, and subsequently apply a k-NN classifier to assess each applicant's creditworthiness based on the clustered data. To boost the effectiveness of our method, we introduce a feature selection strategy. We suggest employing a variable neighborhood search (VNS) technique to identify the most relevant features for the clustering task. We evaluate our methods using several financial datasets, and the results demonstrate their effectiveness. Notably, our findings indicate that VNS significantly improves performance, resulting in increased accuracy across all analyzed datasets.

articleTitle: Fikr: AI Chatbot Powered with Vector Search
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computing, Engineering and Design (ICCED)
abstract: Fikr is a cutting-edge chatbot designed to enhance access to Islamic knowledge by leveraging advanced AI technologies such as vector search and Large Language Models (LLMs), including GPT-3.5. Developed using a combination of Streamlit for the frontend, Flask for the backend, and Firebase for data storage and authentication, Fikr provides users with precise and reliable responses, complete with accurate citations from verified sources such as Hadiths and Quranic verses. A key feature of Fikr is its vector-based search capability, which allows for efficient retrieval of semantically relevant information, improving the accuracy of query responses compared to traditional keyword-based methods. The development process encountered challenges, particularly in data vectorization and ingestion, addressed through iterative troubleshooting and data cleaning methods, resulting in a refined dataset of 33,535 entries. Fikr's answer generation algorithm, incorporating vector database results and LLM -generated responses, ensures that users receive contextually appropriate and well-supported answers. Comparative testing with other AI models, including GPT-4 and Gemini, demonstrated Fikr's superior accuracy and source citation performance.

articleTitle: Next-Gen IoT-Driven Framework for Real-Time Marine Ecosystem Support and Management
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computing, Engineering and Design (ICCED)
abstract: Marine ecosystems face significant threats from pollution, overfishing, and climate change. This research proposes an IoT-based marine monitoring system along with satellite communication, wireless sensor networks (WSNs), unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), marine sensor modules (MSMs), and autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs). Satellite communication provides real-time data flow between remote ocean locations and control centers. WSNs collect environmental data such as water quality, temperature, and pollution levels. UAVs offer aerial surveillance while AUVs scan the seabed and deep-sea habitats. These vehicles respond automatically to detected changes. AI driven analytics process the collected data to detect risks early. When a problem is detected, the system takes accurate actions. It alerts authorities and directs AUVs to investigate the affected areas further. The system helps manage mobile marine protected areas (MMPAs) and supports long-term ecosystem sustainability. This combination of real-time data and autonomous responses protects sensitive environments, such as coral reefs and fish breeding grounds. This IoT-based system ensures proactive solutions for marine conservation and protects ocean ecosystems' health and resilience.

articleTitle: The Role of Perceived Usability, Social Media and Data Security in the Adoption of Fintech Services
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computing, Engineering and Design (ICCED)
abstract: The adoption of financial technology (fintech) has rapidly increased in recent years, particularly in Indonesia, driven by consumer demand for efficient and secure financial transactions. This study analyzes the relationships between social media, perceived usability, and data security in influencing fintech adoption. Utilizing a quantitative methodology, an online survey collected responses from 165 participants in Jakarta. The findings indicate that social media significantly impacts users' decisions to adopt fintech services, while data security is crucial for consumer trust and support for fintech implementation. Although perceived usability is important for enhancing user experience, it shows an insignificant influence on fintech adoption in Indonesia. Therefore, innovation in data security and the development of social media are necessary for promoting fintech adoption in the country

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of SQL and Apache Spark: Time Evaluation in Loan Portfolio Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computing, Engineering and Design (ICCED)
abstract: This paper provides a detailed comparative analysis of SQL and Apache Spark within the context of Loan Portfolio Analysis (LPA), focusing on the data processing efficiency of each approach across different dataset sizes. With the financial industry increasingly dependent on fast, large-scale data processing, understanding the strengths and limitations of these tools is essential. While SQL remains a longstanding solution for data management and querying, Apache Spark's distributed computing capabilities offer substantial advantages, particularly for managing large and complex datasets. Through a series of practical case studies, this study examines the time required for data aggregation and analysis using both SQL and Spark. The findings highlight notable performance differences, with Spark consistently showing increased efficiency when handling larger datasets and complex queries. Such insights are crucial for financial institutions aiming to enhance both operational efficiency and the accuracy of decision-making. This research provides a clear framework for tool selection based on dataset size and complexity, thus supporting institutions in making better-informed decisions regarding data processing practices. Ultimately, this comparative analysis serves as a guide to optimize data handling in the financial sector, aligning processing tools with data needs for improved results and strategic agility.

articleTitle: Cybersecurity Vulnerabilities in Smartwatches as Health Devices using Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computing, Engineering and Design (ICCED)
abstract: Modern technology places a wealth of information at users' fingertips, including health monitoring capabilities through wearable devices such as smartwatches. Smartwatches offer various benefits for human health, such as monitoring heart rate, pulse rate, blood oxygen levels, physical activity reminders, stress levels, sleep analysis, daily step counts and function as digital medical records. This device plays an important role in detecting serious health conditions, such as atrial fibrillation and sleep disorders, by providing early warnings to users to seek medical care immediately. While smartwatches have empowered individuals to be proactive in maintaining health, they also present new challenges, concerns have arisen regarding potential cybersecurity threats related to user privacy and data security. This study aims to identify threats and vulnerabilities associated with the use of smartwatches and assess the risks arising from these vulnerabilities. An in-depth literature review of cyber attack threats and vulnerabilities in the use of smart watches. In addition, this study also proposes mitigation strategies that can be applied to reduce these risks, including improving security protocols and educating users about potential dangers. Thus, this study makes an important contribution to understanding the complexity of risks associated with smartwatch use and provides practical recommendations to mitigate possible negative impacts.

articleTitle: The Relationships Between the Binary Correlation and Accuracy in Logistic Regression for Predicting Employee Attrition
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computing, Engineering and Design (ICCED)
abstract: This research paper examines the accuracy of the logistic regression method in predicting employee attrition. Employee attrition is of particular interest to human resources departments due to its impact on organizational performance and employee satisfaction. Specifically, this study aims to establish the relationships between various control variables and the binary response variable representing employee attrition. Using the popular IBM HR Analytics Employee Dataset, we assess the contribution of each control variable to prediction accuracy. Additionally, we determine the correlation between each control variable and employee attrition data. For binary control variables, we use the phi correlation, while for non-binary control variables, we employ the point-biserial correlation coefficient. Our results reveal a positive correlation between the value of the correlation coefficient and the improvement in prediction accuracy, highlighting an important principle in building logistic regression models for similar cases.

articleTitle: Optimizing Government Funding Allocation with Ensemble Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computing, Engineering and Design (ICCED)
abstract: Given the limited availability of state funds, managing state finances in an effective, efficient, and prudent manner is essential. High demand for additional state funds without sound justification can lead to inefficiencies and poor budget execution. Therefore, decisions regarding the allocation of additional funds should be made selectively and based on historical data reflecting the quality of the work unit in budget management. This research aims to develop a machine learning application to assist decision-makers in recommending additional funding percentages. Utilizing the Budget Implementation Quality Indicator (IKPA) data, we performed feature selection using Principal Component Analysis (PCA), resulting in three selected features. These features were then used to build models with base models (Decision Tree Regression, K-Nearest Neighbor Regression) and ensemble learning methods (Stacking, Bagging, Random Forest, Boosting: AdaBoost, XGBoost, LightGBM). After to-Fold Cross-Validation and hyperparameter tuning, LightGBM demonstrated the lowest error rate with a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.0646 and a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.0520, outperforming XGBoost in predicting additional fund allocation proportions. The application supports informed and accountable financial decision-making, promoting efficient and prudent national financial management. By comparing base models and ensemble techniques, this research provides critical insights into machine learning applications in financial management, driving methodological innovation and advancing the field.

articleTitle: Improving Public Health Disaster Response through Data Analytics by Addressing Gaps in Technology and Resource Allocation
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computing, Engineering and Design (ICCED)
abstract: Natural disasters, including earthquakes, tsunamis, and volcanic eruptions, pose significant and recurrent threats to public health in Indonesia, one of the world's most disaster-prone regions. While conventional disaster management primarily focuses on emergency response, the growing scale and frequency of these events demand a shift towards proactive preparedness using advanced technology. This study addresses a critical gap in Indonesian disaster preparedness: the underutilization of data analytics for enhancing public health response and resource allocation during disasters. By developing an innovative data-driven framework that integrates real-time surveillance, predictive modeling, and machine learning, this research introduces a novel approach to improving disaster preparedness. The proposed framework empowers decision-makers to forecast healthcare needs, optimize resource allocation, and deploy early warning systems with precision. Results demonstrate that predictive modeling achieves up to a 40% improvement in resource allocation efficiency, particularly within the vital first 72 hours post-disaster, where rapid response can significantly reduce mortality and prevent disease outbreaks. This paper highlights the transformative potential of data analytics for disaster resilience, advocating for its integration into Indonesia's public health infrastructure to build a robust and adaptive disaster response system.

articleTitle: Collaborative Architecture-Based Interoperability Framework for Enterprise Operations Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computing, Engineering and Design (ICCED)
abstract: Digitalization is critical for modern organizations, requiring gradual enhancements across departments to accelerate operations and improve service delivery. Businesses often acquire new systems to streamline workflows, enhance efficiency, and boost company growth. The difficulty emerges when businesses utilize multiple systems concurrently to meet demand, often resulting in these systems being unintegrated. Effective communication between systems is vital to facilitate collaboration and integration, ensuring the achievement of business goals. Interoperability refers to a capacity of diverse systems to collaborate, share data, and use information effectively. It acts as a centralized hub, assimilating data from different systems and storage solutions, guaranteeing seamless access throughout the entire enterprise. The PRISMA methodology was applied for the Systematic Literature Review (SLR), allowing for adaptability to the research on interoperability solutions. Multiple strategies and cooperative techniques were also utilized to formulate a concept, model, and architecture referred to as OMEC. This study assists companies or organizations in refining their business processes and operations by implementing an interoperability framework to promote communication and collaboration in their digitization initiatives.

articleTitle: Enhancing Heart Attack Prediction Accuracy by Finding the Best SVM Parameter Value with Fuzzy Logic
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computing, Engineering and Design (ICCED)
abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains a leading cause of mortality globally, with heart disease being a significant contributor. Early detection is crucial for timely intervention through counseling and medication, as delayed diagnosis increases patient morbidity and mortality. However, early-stage detection is challenging due to the complexity of data processing required for accurate predictions. This study employs Fuzzy Logic to optimize Support Vector Machine (SVM) parameters, enhancing the hyperplane's effectiveness and improving prediction accuracy. Utilizing the Heart Disease Classification Dataset from Kaggle, comprising 1,319 entries with eight input and one output field, the standard SVM achieved an 80% overall accuracy, with 73<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> precision for the negative class and 83 % for the positive class, completing the process in 1.362 seconds. In contrast, the SVM optimized with Fuzzy Logic parameters achieved an 89.39% overall accuracy, with 85% precision for the negative class and 92 % for the positive class, taking 1.1 seconds. This research demonstrates that Fuzzy Logic optimization significantly enhances SVM performance in heart attack prediction.

articleTitle: A Decision Tree Approach to Understanding How Being Phubbed by Friends Differs from Being Phubbed by Children
publicationTitle: 2024 10th International Conference on Computing, Engineering and Design (ICCED)
abstract: Smartphones have become an integral part of daily life. However, unhealthy attachments to smartphones have resulted in phubbing, which can be particularly disruptive for social interactions, psychological well-being, loneliness, relationship satisfaction, and self-esteem. This study combined data from two related studies to compare the impact of being phubbed by one's friends against the impact of being phubbed by one's children. Using data mining techniques, the study found that parents with lower self-esteem are more affected by their children's repetitive phubbing than young people with low self-esteem are by their friends' repetitive phubbing. Additionally, parents with low psychological well-being are more impacted by occasional phubbing from their children than young people with low psychological well-being are by occasional phubbing from friends. Young people with high psychological well-being are more affected by repetitive phubbing from friends compared to parents with high psychological well-being affected by their children's repetitive phubbing. Furthermore, young people with poor psychological well-being and low relationship satisfaction are more affected by infrequent phubbing from friends than parents in a similar state are by infrequent phubbing from their children. Youth with low friendship satisfaction and loneliness are particularly affected by friends' infrequent phubbing. This study demonstrates the need to raise awareness of the diverse experiences of phubbing to promote healthy smartphone use and mitigate psychological and emotional distress.
